14	CASE OD2-HO-SEQ-1 (SEQ, technical): Soft pedals at Eastgate depot
15	Setting: Larkspur Parcel Co. runs 140 light delivery vans from three depots: Eastgate (38 vans, LK-201 to LK-238), Millbrook (44) and Harrow Lane (58). Eastgate's vans are maintained in an in-house brake bay, which was closed for refurbishment from 4 August to 19 September. In 2025 the company changed several things in quick succession: a new front-pad supplier (Tessaro Friction) from 1 July, a defect-reporting app (FleetCheck) at all depots from 1 August, and a new set of hilly delivery routes (Upper Wend) run from Eastgate starting 1 September. Since early September, Eastgate drivers have been reporting brake problems, and one van nearly crashed.
16	Presenting request: The Regional Operations Director wants a decision by Friday. What is causing the cluster of soft-pedal and fade complaints at Eastgate, and what should the company do this week? She is minded to discipline drivers who keep complaining and retrain everyone on descent braking.
17	INITIAL EVIDENCE
18	E1 [stage S1] Email from Mariana Selby, Regional Operations Director, to fleet analyst, 13 Oct (leadership-account): Subject: Eastgate brakes – need a call by Friday. Since early September Eastgate drivers have logged 27 soft-pedal or fade complaints. On 9 October LK-209 lost most of its braking on the Carrow Hill descent. The driver stopped it with gears and the handbrake, and nobody was hurt. LK-209 is parked. My view: this started the week we launched Upper Wend, and Upper Wend is the only hilly work we have. I think drivers are riding the brakes all the way down. I'm minded to issue written warnings to the repeat complainers (some have filed three or four) and put everyone through descent retraining. Tell me if I'm wrong, with evidence.
19	E2 [stage S1] FleetCheck defect-report extract, brake categories, 1 Jul–31 Oct (system-record): Soft pedal / fade category. Eastgate (38 vans): 0 reports Jul–Aug; 27 reports Sep–Oct on 11 vans (count; first–last report): LK-203 (3; 4 Sep–21 Oct), LK-205 (2; 11 Sep–9 Oct), LK-207 (3; 2 Sep–27 Oct), LK-209 (4; 8 Sep–9 Oct), LK-211 (2; 15 Sep–16 Oct), LK-217 (3; 3–22 Sep), LK-220 (2; 18 Sep–24 Oct), LK-222 (2; 9 Sep–13 Oct), LK-224 (2; 5–23 Sep), LK-230 (2; 22 Sep–30 Oct), LK-233 (2; 26 Sep–28 Oct). Millbrook (44 vans) and Harrow Lane (58 vans) together: 2 reports Sep–Oct. Typical free text: 'fine at the top, pedal long by the bottom of Carrow Hill'. Note: FleetCheck replaced paper defect sheets at all three depots on 1 Aug.
20	E3 [stage S1] Interview notes, Tom Rudd, Eastgate depot manager, 14 Oct (manager-account): Rudd: 'Upper Wend went live on 1 September. Long downhill runs, Carrow Hill is the worst, and it takes eight or nine vans a day. Before that we were all flat suburbs. The timing speaks for itself.' On maintenance: the in-house brake bay was closed for refurbishment 4 Aug–19 Sep. Workshop coordinator Dev Okafor booked brake services that fell due in that period with Northfield Motor Services or Calder Road Garage, whichever had a slot first. 'Both fitted the Tessaro pads we supplied and did the standard two-year fluid change off the same job sheet, so that's not it.' The fleet engineer checked three complaint vans on 26 Sep and found no fault. Okafor is on leave until November.
21	E4 [stage S1] Meeting note, Priya Nandakumar, driver and union representative, 15 Oct (staff-account): 'This isn't about how we drive. Plenty of us have done Upper Wend, and we all take turns on it. What changed is the pads. Head office switched to Tessaro in July because they were cheaper, and since then you hear squealing everywhere. Cheap pads on steep hills, they cook. And now people are scared to report in case they get a warning.' She asked that drivers who reported faults not be disciplined. Asked which vans have which pads or where vans were serviced, she said she did not know.
22	E5 [stage S1] Procurement change record PCR-0417 with fleet engineering note (change-record): PCR-0417, effective 1 Jul: front brake pads for all depots switched from the previous supplier to Tessaro Friction. Pads are fitted as vans fall due for them, not as a campaign. By 30 Sep, 81 of 140 vans (58%) had Tessaro pads. Fleet engineering note, 6 Oct: 'Noise/squeal reports fleet-wide: 5 in Apr–Jun, 21 in Jul–Sep, 17 of the 21 on Tessaro-fitted vans. Caution: Tessaro vans are by definition the ones with freshly fitted pads, and we have no noise data on fresh pads of the old brand. FleetCheck also replaced paper defect sheets from 1 Aug.'
23	CATALOGUE (full contents)
24	C1 [stage S1] Telematics braking-event summary by depot, August–October - Fleet telematics platform report (telemetry): Harsh-braking events per 100 km. Eastgate: Aug 2.4, Sep 3.3, Oct 3.2. Millbrook: 2.5, 2.6, 2.7. Harrow Lane: 2.3, 2.2, 2.6. Eastgate Upper Wend route segments only, Sep–Oct: 4.6. Average speed at the top of the Carrow Hill descent: 31 mph (limit 30). Per-van and per-driver breakdowns are not enabled on the current licence, so events cannot be attributed to individual vans or drivers.
25	C2 [stage S1] Tessaro Friction batch test certificates and supplier letter - Tessaro Friction account manager, letter dated 20 Oct (vendor-account): Certificates attached for batches T-0612 and T-0703. Letter: 'Both batches tested within our published friction band at 100–350°C, and the fade test was passed. We supply more than 40 fleet customers and have no other fade reports for these batches. Pad material does not affect pedal travel unless pads are worn or wrongly fitted. We are happy to support any joint investigation.' The certificates are the supplier's own tests. No independent test is on file.
26	C3 [stage S1] Calder Road Garage job cards, stores records and correspondence for Larkspur vans, August–September - Calder Road Garage, supplied on request (document): Job cards 6 Aug–18 Sep, 12 vans: LK-201/204/206/210/212/215/218/221/225/228/231/236. Each card: front pads fitted (customer-supplied Tessaro), brake fluid changed 'from sealed 1 L bottles', pressure bleed, road test passed. Stores record: brake fluid bought in 1 L bottles and rotated by date. LK-218 card notes 'nearside slide pin seized, freed and greased'. Invoices match the cards. Correspondence: invoices and booking emails only. No warranty returns.
27	C4 [stage S1] Fleet engineer's inspection notes on three complaint vans, 26 September - A. Brandt, Larkspur fleet engineer (expert-account): Vans inspected: LK-203, LK-211, LK-230. Pad thickness 10–11 mm, discs within limits, no fluid leaks, reservoir level correct, fluid clear. Pedal firm in a static test. A 10 km road test on flat roads found no fault. Conclusion: 'No mechanical fault found. Pattern fits heat build-up from riding the brakes on long descents; suggest a descent-technique briefing.' Brandt notes that Eastgate has no brake-fluid boiling-point tester and none was used.
28	C5 [stage S1] Upper Wend route survey: gradients and descent lengths - Route planning team survey, August (document): Carrow Hill: 1.8 km at an average 9%, with a sharp left at the foot. Mill Brow: 1.1 km at 7%. Wend Lane: 0.9 km at 8%. A typical Upper Wend route has 4–6 significant descents and 70–90 drops per shift. Planner's note: 'Steepest work in the network; recommend lower gear on Carrow Hill.' No brake-temperature measurements were taken during the survey.
29	C6 [stage S1] Fleet maintenance system export: Eastgate service history and daily van assignments, June–October - Larkspur fleet maintenance system (system-record): Brake services (front pads + fluid change) by workshop. Northfield Motor Services, 4 Aug–12 Sep: 13 vans, LK-203/205/207/209/211/214/217/220/222/224/227/230/233; pads Tessaro T-0612 ×7, T-0703 ×6. Calder Road Garage, 6 Aug–18 Sep: 12 vans; T-0612 ×5, T-0703 ×7. In-house bay, Jun–Jul and 22 Sep–28 Oct: 13 vans; Tessaro ×11, previous brand ×2. Remarks: LK-217 and LK-224 'warranty return to Northfield 24 Sep, see garage paperwork'; both back in the pool 25 Sep, with 7 and 6 Upper Wend days since then. Sep–Oct assignments: vans are issued from a common pool, and each of the 38 vans ran Upper Wend on 9–16 days. The 27 soft-pedal reports came from 19 drivers. Those drivers also logged 604 days in non-Northfield vans, 141 of them on Upper Wend, with no brake reports.
30	C7 [stage S1] Eastgate driver interviews, six drivers, 14 October - Notes by Eastgate depot supervisor (staff-account): Four of the six said some vans 'go long on Carrow Hill' and others don't, and two named LK-207 and LK-209. Two said they use a low gear on descents; four said they 'brake on and off'. One said: 'I had 205 go soft on Mill Brow, and the next day I took 212 down the same hill and it was fine.' All six said they had become reluctant to report after hearing that warnings were being considered. None knew where individual vans had been serviced.
31	C8 [stage S1] FleetCheck app rollout record and defect-report volumes by category, all depots, May–October - FleetCheck product owner (system-record): Go-live on 1 Aug at all three depots, replacing paper sheets. Defect reports per month, all categories, fleet-wide: May 61, Jun 58, Jul 64, Aug 103, Sep 112, Oct 108. The rise is spread across categories: lights +71%, tyres +58%, bodywork +80%, noise +64%. The app records van ID and free text; driver ID is optional. Product owner: 'Reporting is easier now, and we expected volumes to rise everywhere.'
32	C9 [stage S1] Northfield Motor Services job cards, stores records and correspondence for Larkspur vans, August–September - Northfield Motor Services, supplied on request (document): Job cards 4 Aug–12 Sep, 13 vans: front pads (customer-supplied Tessaro) and brake fluid change. Fluid source per card: LK-214 (11 Sep) and LK-227 (12 Sep) 'new 20 L drum, opened 10 Sep'; the other 11 'bulk drum, bay 3'. Stores log: bay 3 drum opened 14 Mar; 1 Aug stock check 'cap missing, replaced'; drum emptied 9 Sep. Warranty card 24 Sep, LK-217 and LK-224, 'long pedal on hills': fluid boiling point 152°C and 149°C; sealed stock reads 255°C. Technician: 'Fluid has taken on water. Low-boiling fluid can vaporise in hot calipers on long descents, and the pedal goes soft.' Fluid renewed from sealed stock; pads not disturbed. Email to D. Okafor, 25 Sep: 'Recommend rechecking the other Larkspur vans we did before 10 Sep.' No reply on file.
33	C10 [stage S1] Regional weather record, daily maximum temperatures, August–October - Regional meteorological service (external-data): Eastgate area daily maximum temperatures: August mean 24°C (peak 31°C on 14 Aug), September mean 19°C, October mean 14°C. No days above 30°C after 20 August. Rain on 22 days in September and 19 days in October. Values come from the nearest automatic station, 6 km from the depot.
34	C11 [stage S1] Tessaro pad tender evaluation and pricing file, May - Larkspur procurement (financial-record): Three bidders were evaluated. Tessaro scored 78/100 (price 40/40, technical 30/40, references 8/20). The incumbent scored 71/100 (price 26/40, technical 34/40, references 11/20). Projected saving from the switch: £21,400 a year on front pads. Technical scoring was done from datasheets, with no fleet trial. Approved by the procurement lead and the fleet engineer on 28 May.
35	C12 [stage S1] Driver training records: descent-braking module completion, all depots - Larkspur learning management system (document): Descent-braking e-learning module, introduced 2024 (20 minutes, no practical assessment). Completion: Eastgate 31 of 44 drivers (70%), Millbrook 38 of 51 (75%), Harrow Lane 49 of 67 (73%). At Eastgate, 13 of the 19 drivers who filed soft-pedal reports have completed it, and 18 of the 25 who have not filed any have. Completion is not checked before route assignment.
36	C13 [stage S1] Millbrook and Harrow Lane brake defect reports, July–October - FleetCheck extract, other depots (system-record): Soft pedal: 2 reports. MB-114, 12 Sep: master cylinder seal leaking, replaced, no recurrence. HL-330, 3 Oct: no fault found, no recurrence. Noise/squeal: 14 reports, 11 of them on Tessaro-fitted vans, mostly within three weeks of pad fitting. Pulling: 3 reports, all traced to tyre pressures. Neither depot has routes with descents comparable to Upper Wend.
37	C14 [stage S1] Eastgate in-house workshop job cards, June–October - Eastgate workshop (document): Jun–Jul: 6 brake services (LK-202/208/213/219/226/229). 22 Sep–28 Oct, after the bay reopened: 7 brake services (LK-216/223/232/234/235/237/238). All 13: front pads fitted (Tessaro, except LK-202 and LK-208, which got the previous brand), fluid changed from sealed 1 L bottles, vacuum bleed, road test passed. No boiling-point testing equipment is listed in the bay inventory.
38	C15 [stage S1] Insurer's incident file for the 9 October Carrow Hill near-miss - Larkspur's motor insurer, claims assessor (document): Vehicle LK-209. Dashcam: the van enters the Carrow Hill descent at 29 mph, holds 24–28 mph for 1.2 km, then speeds up to 37 mph approaching the junction. It stops 6 m past the give-way line using the handbrake and second gear. Driver statement: 'The pedal went to the floor about two-thirds of the way down; it had been fine at the top.' Assessor: 'Driving within limits before the event; vehicle inspection pending.' No third-party damage.
39	CANDIDATES
40	H1: Eastgate drivers' braking technique on descents is causing the soft-pedal and fade complaints.
41	H2: The Tessaro pads introduced in July are defective or unsuited to Eastgate's work and are causing the soft-pedal and fade complaints.
42	H3: Brake work done at an outside garage during the in-house bay closure left the affected vans with a brake-system fault that is causing the complaints.
43	H4: The descents on the Upper Wend routes are overheating brakes that are otherwise in sound condition.
44	H5: The complaint cluster reflects easier reporting through FleetCheck rather than a real change in brake performance.
45	R1: Brake fluid put into the affected vans during bay-closure servicing -> Eastgate soft-pedal and fade complaints (causes)
46	R2: Tessaro pads fitted to Eastgate vans -> Eastgate soft-pedal and fade complaints (causes)
47	R3: Switch to Tessaro pads -> Fleet-wide rise in noise/squeal reports (causes)
48	R4: Eastgate drivers' braking technique on descents -> Eastgate soft-pedal and fade complaints (causes)
49	A1: Take every van that had brake work at Northfield Motor Services during the bay closure out of service until its brake fluid has been boiling-point tested and renewed from sealed stock, then return it to the pool.
50	A2: Issue written warnings to drivers who have filed repeated brake complaints, and require all Eastgate drivers to complete descent-braking retraining before driving Upper Wend again.
51	A3: Switch fleet brake-pad orders back to the previous supplier from the next procurement cycle to cut squeal and noise reports.
52	A4: Add a brake-fluid boiling-point check to the next scheduled service of the Eastgate vans that were not serviced at Northfield.

answers.justification: Vans come from a shared pool (C6). The 19 complaining drivers logged 604 days, 141 of them on Upper Wend, in non-Northfield vans with no brake reports (C6, C7). Their training completion matches that of non-complainers (C12), and the LK-209 dashcam shows it was driven within limits (C15).

The Calder Road and in-house vans got the same Tessaro batches (T-0612/T-0703) and ran Upper Wend just as often, with zero soft-pedal reports (C3, C6, C14, E2). LK-217 and LK-224 stopped complaining after only their fluid was renewed and the pads were left alone (C9).

All 11 complaint vans are exactly the Northfield vans filled from the bay-3 bulk drum, which was open since March and had a missing cap (E2, C6, C9). The two warranty-return vans measured boiling points of 152°C and 149°C against 255°C for sealed stock, and their reports stopped after the fluid was renewed (C9, E2, C6).

The descents are a necessary trigger (C5, C15), but the 'otherwise sound brakes' part is contradicted. Vans with sound fluid ran the same descents without complaints, and the affected vans had water-contaminated fluid (C6, C9). Weather was cooling over the period (C10).

FleetCheck went live at all depots on 1 Aug (C8), yet soft-pedal reports cluster on specific Northfield vans (E2, C6). They are backed by measured fluid degradation (C9) and a near-miss on dashcam (C15), with zero reports at Eastgate in August under the app (E2).

The evidence covers every element: fluid fitted before symptoms appeared (C6, E2), a documented mechanism (C9), exact covariation with the bulk-drum vans (C6, C9), rivals ruled out by same-pad/same-route/same-driver comparisons (C3, C6, C14), and an intervention in which renewing the fluid on LK-217/224 ended their complaints (C9, C6, E2).
Seventeen Tessaro-fitted non-Northfield Eastgate vans (C3, C14) had no soft-pedal reports despite 9–16 Upper Wend days each (C6), and the pads were left untouched in the fix that worked (C9).

Noise reports rose and most were on Tessaro vans (E5, C13). However, Tessaro vans are by definition the freshly padded ones with no fresh-pad baseline for the old brand, and FleetCheck raised reporting across all categories (E5, C8).

The same drivers on the same routes had no problems in non-Northfield vans (C6, C7), training does not separate complainers from non-complainers (C12), and the LK-209 driving was within limits (C15). The harsh-braking rise in C1 cannot be attributed to individual vans or drivers.

This directly addresses the established cause, a safety hazard that has already produced a near-miss (C9, C15). The garage itself recommended rechecking these vans (C9), and the action is proportionate and reversible.

The drivers' reports correctly flagged real faulty vans (C6, C9). Disciplining them would punish the wrong party and suppress safety reporting, which drivers already say they are afraid to do (E4, C7).
The link between the pads and noise is only an association, confounded by fresh fitting and the FleetCheck rollout (E5, C8). The pads are not implicated in the soft-pedal problem (C3, C14).

This is a low-cost confirmatory check, since Eastgate has no tester (C4, C14). However, the non-Northfield vans used sealed fluid and have had no complaints (C3, C14, C6), so it is reasonable but not urgent.
The Northfield bulk-drum match, the boiling-point readings and the outcome of the fluid-renewal intervention (C6, C9, E2) together justify committing to A1 now.
